content.title: About
content.content: Cereal, cinnamon toast is a dry whole‑grain wheat flake coated with aromatic cinnamon and sugar. It is designed for a quick breakfast: just add milk or yogurt and wait a few minutes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first ready‑to‑eat flakes appeared in the United States in the early 20th century as a convenient way to consume grain.
The cinnamon used in this product is rich in antioxidants and gives it a warm, distinctive aroma.
The formula often includes whole grains, increasing fiber content compared with regular sweet cereals.
The product is marketed as a “5‑minute breakfast” and is popular among busy consumers.
Packaging is usually made from recyclable plastic, reducing its environmental footprint.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Whole‑grain flakes provide sustained energy and help maintain satiety.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestive health and contributes to normal cholesterol levels.

items.title: Contains cinnamon antioxidants
items.content: Cinnamon has anti‑inflammatory properties and may aid glucose metabolism.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The product contains virtually no fat, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Fortified with B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamins B1, B2 and B6 help support the nervous system and energy metabolism.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Sweetened cereals can contain a notable amount of sugar, which is undesirable for people with diabetes or those trying to lose weight.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Made from wheat, the product is not suitable for individuals with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Possible additives
items.content: Some versions may contain artificial flavors and preservatives that could trigger reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Overconsumption
items.content: Large portions can lead to excess calorie and sugar intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Place a serving of flakes in a bowl, pour milk, yogurt, or a plant‑based drink over them, stir and wait 2–3 minutes. You can add fresh fruit, nuts, or honey for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the cereal in its original package or an airtight container in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. When stored properly, it remains fresh for up to 12 months.
